title: The Shell and the Chimney
skyStory: The first quarter moon steps into Cancer, sixty-one percent lit, and immediately wants to go home. Cancer is the crab sign, the homebody, the one who carries its house on its back. The moon finds a cozy shell and settles in. Down on Earth, every chimney gets a little extra smoke and every porch light switches on a few minutes earlier than usual.

reading: The cabin is calling you home today, in every sense. You might find yourself drawn to old photos, familiar music, a favourite worn-out sweater. Go with it. A Cancer moon is a reminder that the place you come back to matters as much as the places you go.

In the evening, do one small thing to make your space feel more like the cabin in your head. A lamp in a new spot. A candle. A blanket on the couch arranged just so. The Tiger, it turns out, also loves a warm den. Let yourself sink into it without a list or a plan. Receiving comfort is still receiving. It still counts.
joel.mission: Move one lamp, candle or blanket to make your home feel more like a cabin, then sit in that spot for ten minutes.
joel.omen: A porch light on in daylight. It means home is waiting for you, warm and ready, whenever you need it.

reading: The crab is a shore creature, and today the moon has moved into its sign, so your territory feels especially strong. You will want to tidy your nest, call someone you love, or simply sit by the water if the weather lets you. All three are correct.

Late afternoon, a memory will float up of a place where you felt completely safe. Maybe a kitchen. Maybe a beach. Maybe a room with a particular smell. Tell Joel about it tonight in three sentences. The [[Ten of Cups]] is not in your spread, but it wanders in today with a blanket and a cup of tea, saying home is a feeling you can carry.
nancy.mission: Describe your safest childhood place to Joel tonight in exactly three sentences, no more, no less.
nancy.omen: A crab, shell or anchor on a sign or label. It means you are carrying home with you everywhere today.

together.text: Cancer moon homecoming. Each of you describe one room from your childhood in three sentences. The other must guess one object that was definitely in that room. Correct guesses earn a cosmic gold star. Wrong guesses earn a story.
